analysis.title: October 22: Equities Selloff Sparks Haven Rally
key_insights: Global risk sentiment deteriorated on AI capital spending concerns and escalating Middle East tensions, driving an equity sell-off, a rally in government bonds and broad EM currency weakness.

US Treasuries rallied across the curve (2y -16.6bp, 10y -16.6bp, 30y -12.9bp). The 7y fell 18.1bp and the 10y yield dropped below 5% for the first time in nearly a month. Short covering in Treasury futures reinforced the move.
Inflation breakevens tightened across the curve (2y -2.2bp, 10y -2.8bp, 30y -2.4bp), reflecting a shift in attention toward growth risks despite higher energy prices.
Markets reduced expectations for additional Fed tightening, with traders no longer fully pricing another hike before year-end.

US equities fell (S&P 500 -1.2%, Nasdaq -2.6%) after disappointing reactions to large-cap technology earnings renewed concerns over the sustainability of AI-related investment. Information Technology and Communication Services each fell 3.0%, while Consumer Staples rose 3.1% and Utilities 2.0%.
VIX rose 14.1% to 19.03 as investors cut exposure to growth-sensitive assets.

Brent rose 3.8% and WTI 2.4% on Middle East tensions and suggestions of possible further action against Iran. Gold fell 2.8%, silver 5.9% and Bitcoin 4.1%, so haven demand stayed concentrated in government bonds and select currencies.

The dollar weakened modestly (DXY -0.2% to 101.62) as falling Treasury yields cut support from rate differentials. JPY led the G10 (USD/JPY -0.9%), followed by CHF (-0.5%). The dollar's response contrasted with earlier geopolitical stress, when elevated US yields supported it.

Risk-sensitive currencies lagged: NZD/USD -0.3% and AUD/USD -0.1%. CAD and NOK gained on oil (USD/CAD -0.3%, USD/NOK -0.3%). New Zealand Q3 inflation was 3.7% y/y (consensus 3.8%), but firm core inflation led local economists to expect a more aggressive RBNZ tightening path.

Euro area: German bonds rallied about 8bp in a near-parallel shift, while French and Italian bonds sold off. 10y OAT/Bund, BTP/Bund and Bono/Bund spreads closed about 15bp, 9bp and 6bp wider. MS attributes the move to idiosyncratic French factors, Middle East tensions and weaker equities, with no single new catalyst.
Euro markets priced out about 5bp of hikes for the December ECB meeting and 7bp for February, even as oil and gas hit new highs. Euro CPI inflation swaps fell about 3bp at the 2y and 5y points.
Gilts rallied (30y about -7bp, 2y about -3bp) and UK hike expectations were priced out, to a lesser extent than in the euro area.

Japan: JGBs ended in a bull-flattening move (10y -1.0bp to 2.88%, 30y -3.5bp to 3.89%, 2y unchanged at 1.90%). The 5-11y liquidity enhancement auction, with issuance cut by JPY150bn, was digested smoothly.
Asia ex-Japan: most currencies weakened and rates mostly rallied. KOSPI fell 3.5%, the Hang Seng 3%, TAIEX 1.8%. TWD fell alongside $2.7bn of foreign equity outflows.
Korea: BoK held at 3.00% unanimously and flagged upward revisions to 2027 growth and inflation forecasts and a higher neutral rate. Korea 1-2y NDIRS yields rose 3bp in a bear-flattening move.
Philippines: BSP hiked 50bp to 5.50% versus 5.25% expected, signalled it is open to more hikes and expects inflation to accelerate further. PHP closed 0.3% weaker and the 10y RPGB sold off 4bp.

Turkey's central bank cut its one-week repo rate 100bp to 36%, in line with consensus. EGP hit a record low against USD in offshore trading. ZAR was the weakest CEEMEA currency (USD/ZAR +0.8%) despite a rally in South African bonds on the Treasury buyback announcement.

LatAm: the Brazilian DI curve underperformed ahead of this weekend's election, with Jan 28 and Jan 29 DIs selling off about 14bp. MXN fell about 0.17% after a hotter-than-expected mid-October CPI print.
US initial jobless claims were 194k (consensus 200k, MS forecast 195k, prior 199k). The four-week average has declined about 10k over the past month.
Day ahead: MS estimates the US manufacturing ISM index falls 1.5 points to 53.0. The Philadelphia Fed ISM-equivalent measure fell from 58.1 to 49.6, its lowest since February.

sector_views.rationale: Defensive sectors outperformed in the sell-off, with Staples up 3.1%. This is an observed move, not an MS recommendation.
Utilities rose 2.0% as defensives outperformed. This is an observed move, not an MS recommendation.
IT fell 3.0% on concerns over AI-related capital spending and large-cap tech earnings reactions. This is an observed move, not an MS recommendation.

risk_factors: Sustainability of AI-related capital spending and large-cap tech earnings.
Middle East escalation and regional energy supply, including possible further action against Iran.
French bond stress and widening peripheral spreads.
Higher energy prices feeding inflation in Asia, Europe and EM.
vol_and_positioning: VIX rose 14.1% to 19.03 as investors reduced exposure to growth-sensitive assets.
Short covering in Treasury futures reinforced the US rates rally.
Foreign equity outflows: $2.7bn in Taiwan and $33mn in Korea.
The XCCY basis widened in 5y+ sectors in Japan.
geopolitical: Escalating Middle East tensions lifted oil, with suggestions of possible further action against Iran and concerns over regional energy supplies.
Egypt's pound hit a record low against USD offshore, pressured by Middle East tensions and higher energy prices.
Brazil's election runoff is this weekend and the DI curve sold off ahead of it.
Hungary faces pressure from higher energy costs and uncertainty around plans for euro-area accession.
Colombia's budget faced a setback, adding domestic political noise.
